after: A learned model counts as engineering evidence only when it serves a stated later task and a checked decision. Its name proves nothing.

after: Suppose a specialized design wins only when all inputs fit in a small memory. Then that memory size is part of the result.

after: A compiler result, an accelerator result and a layout result are separate evidence. They join up only when their interfaces, formats, sizes and test conditions match.

before: Likewise, a kernel built for contiguous arrays needs a valid alternative, or a rejection path, for an array whose elements are spaced further apart in memory (a larger **stride**).
after: Likewise, a kernel built for arrays stored side by side needs a plan for spaced-out arrays. The spacing between elements is the **stride**. The kernel must handle a larger stride correctly, or refuse it.

before: A cost model should rank candidates only after their behavior and conditions are established, or clearly mark rankings that include candidates still awaiting validation.
after: A cost model should rank only candidates whose behaviour is already checked. Otherwise it must mark which ranked candidates are still unchecked.

before: The claim must say what was checked, under which assumptions, and whether an unresolved case was rejected, re-checked exactly, or accepted without a guarantee.
after: The claim must say what was checked and under which assumptions. It must also say what happened to unresolved cases: rejected, re-checked exactly, or accepted without a guarantee.

before: If nine runs fail and one gives a good result, reporting only the survivor hides the odds and cost of getting a usable output.
after: Say nine runs fail and one gives a good result. Reporting only that one hides the odds, and the cost, of getting a usable output.

before: If a constraint violation is treated as just a poor score, the search can keep picking invalid outputs whenever another score part makes up for it.
after: Treat a broken rule as just a low score, and the search can keep picking invalid outputs. Another part of the score can make up for the break.

before: A compiler's improved operator, or an accelerator generator's favorable model, must still fit a complete application with data movement, numerical quality and preparation costs.
after: A faster compiled step, or a good result from an accelerator generator, must still fit the whole application. That includes data movement, numerical quality and set-up costs.

before: A system can have enough capacity and high bandwidth, yet still be slow for a chain of small reads that each wait for the last.
after: A system can have room to spare and fast links, yet still be slow. A chain of small reads, each waiting for the one before, is enough to do it.

before: An optimizer that takes ten minutes but needs ninety minutes of cleanup is not a ten-minute path to an accepted layout.
after: An optimizer that runs for ten minutes but needs ninety minutes of clean-up is not a ten-minute route to a finished layout.

before: Injecting one isolated bit flip does not show protection against a failing chip, a burst across several words, or a lasting logic defect.
after: Testing one flipped bit does not show protection against bigger faults. A failing chip, a burst across several words, or a lasting defect each need their own test.

before: Whether that difference leaks useful information depends on what an observer can measure, on noise and repetitions, and on what else they know.
after: Whether that difference leaks anything useful depends on the observer. It depends on what they can measure, on noise and repeats, and on what else they know.
